history.summary: Devarayanadurga is a fortified hill station (~1,204 m) near Tumakuru with two Narasimha temples: the Bhoga Narasimha at the foot of the hill (attributed by local legend to Chola-period work / sage Durvasa's installation; some sources date it to the 9th century) and the Yoga Narasimha (Lakshminarasimha) temple higher up, built in Dravidian style by Kanthirava Narasaraja Wodeyar of Mysore and repaired in 1858 by Krishnaraja Wodeyar III (per the Karnataka archaeology department). The ancient names of the hill were Karigiri / Simhadri / Siddhagiri; the fort has seven tiers and gateways and was a Vijayanagara-era military base. The name Devarayanadurga comes from Devaraja, the Mysore commander who took the fort from the bandit Jataka in 1608. The Karnataka archaeology department coordinates for the Lakshminarasimha temple (13.3735, 77.2074) are used here. Festival calendar and opening hours are not officially published; listed festivals/hours are typical (verify locally). Town correction: the CSV 'Tumkur' is the district town; the site is Devarayanadurga, ~15 km from Tumakuru.

name: Devarayanadurga Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple
town_description: Devarayanadurga is a hill town and fort about 15 km from Tumakuru, rising to ~1,204 m. It is a popular trekking and pilgrimage destination with the Yoga Narasimha and Bhoga Narasimha temples, the Namada Chilume spring, and a state forest nursery of medicinal plants.

travel.road: ~15 km east of Tumakuru; ~65 km from Bengaluru via NH-48

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; pleasant for trekking
visitor_information.opening_hours: Typical hours ~6:00 AM-12:00 PM and 5:00-8:30 PM (verify locally)
